value: Synthetic plan for a synthetic project. The metrics are defined against records that exist; the collection cycle has never run on a real cycle.

The observation population is seven points. No trend line is drawn from seven points and the plan says so; the 'trending down review over review' target on MET-04 is an intent, not an expectation that the data supports.
MET-02 publishes two denominators because two exist, which is a weakness of the metric rather than of the data. It is recorded rather than resolved by picking the flattering one.
MET-06 at a population of 6 cannot support a percentage. The control limit on it is therefore not a useful signal yet, and the plan says so in its own action_on_breach.

The population bias towards the cell-voltage chain means every metric is flattered by the one part of the project that was completed. A metric that cannot see the parts that were not done will look good precisely because they were not done.
No human reviewed this plan. Its metrics are the author's choices, and a metric set chosen by the person being measured is the oldest problem in process measurement.

analysis_method.analysis_cadence: monthly for MET-04 and MET-06; at each gate for MET-01, MET-02 and MET-03; fortnightly for MET-05
analysis_method.control_limit_rule: A metric breaches when its value crosses the control limit stated for it. A single breach triggers the action_on_breach field. Three consecutive breaches of the same metric trigger a PIM.3 improvement proposal.
analysis_method.how_a_chart_is_derived: Every point on every chart is one OBS-* record in this plan's observations array, with its derivation naming the records it was counted from. A trend line is drawn only where the points exist. Where the points do not exist the chart says so and is not drawn; an unsupported trend is worse than an empty chart because it reads as a result.
analysis_method.method: Simple arithmetic over the counted population, with the numerator and the denominator both stated in every report. No index, no weighting and no composite score: a composite lets a good number hide a bad one, and the corpus's history is a record of exactly that.
analysis_method.who_performs_the_analysis: project_manager for MET-01, MET-02 and MET-05; quality_engineer for MET-03, MET-04 and MET-06; reviewer_adversarial attends and challenges

measurement_population.known_population_bias: The population is biased toward the cell-voltage safety chain because that is where the corpus is dense. A metric such as 'requirements with a verification measure' will therefore look better than the project deserves, because the records it counts are concentrated in the one chain that was completed. This bias is stated here so that no one reads a favourable number as representative.
measurement_population.sample_size_assumption: The population is assumed to be between 150 and 400 artifacts over the programme, which is consistent with the 205 records this corpus holds at the plan's start date. If the population exceeded 1000 the 100% rule would be reviewed, because at that size manual review is the constraint and not the collection.
measurement_population.sampling_rule: 100% of artifacts at every baseline and every revision. No sampling of artifacts: a sampling rule for the thing being reviewed is the defect this plan exists to prevent. Executions are sampled at 100% as well; the population is small enough that sampling buys nothing and hides everything.
what_is_excluded: Any measurement of the product's behaviour. This plan measures the development process and never the product.
Any record produced by an automated tool and not reviewed by a person. Counting machine output as process performance would let the tooling grade itself.
Any observation before the plan's start date, because there is no consistent collection for it.
Any observation whose collection rule was not followed. Missing observations are recorded as missing, not imputed.
what_is_measured: Every engineering artifact produced by the project, once per baseline and once per revision
Every verification measure once per planning cycle
Every execution record once per run
Every review record once per review pass
Every supporting-process instance once per occurrence
Every project risk entry once per review cycle

metrics.action_on_breach: Downgrade the status to the state the records actually support and record the correction. Do not author a record to make the number improve.
metrics.baseline: 13 expectations marked mapped with no backing record, corrected 2026-09-29
metrics.control_limit: any expectation carrying a mapped status with no named record
metrics.definition: The number of applicable process and ISO-part expectations whose recorded status is backed by a corpus record, over the number applicable.
metrics.formula_or_rule: count(status is backed by a record) / count(applicable)
metrics.metric_name: Standards-mapped coverage of the applicable process and ISO part inventory
metrics.target: 1.0 with every mapped status backed by a named record

metrics.action_on_breach: Author a measure with a declared oracle basis for the uncovered requirements. Do not add a link from an existing measure that does not actually cover the requirement.
metrics.baseline: 41 of 48 requirement artifacts uncovered at the plan's start date
metrics.control_limit: below 95 percent, or any safety-domain requirement below COVERED-INDIRECT
metrics.definition: The number of requirement artifacts with a verification measure reachable directly or through an allocated child, over the number of requirement artifacts.

metrics.action_on_breach: Raise a finding against the execution record and reset the claim to the state the evidence supports. Never edit a past execution record to make it consistent.
metrics.baseline: 100 percent; 25 records with 13 host or simulation runs and 12 synthetic fixtures or none
metrics.control_limit: any dishonest pair, or any increase in actual-run claims between consecutive collections
metrics.definition: The number of execution records whose execution_kind and outcome are mutually honest, over the number of execution records. An execution claiming a real run without an evidence reference, or a synthetic fixture claiming a pass without a fixture, is dishonest.
metrics.target: 100 percent, and no increase in actual-run claims without evidence

metrics.action_on_breach: Open a problem-resolution record against the finding and block the gate it belongs to.
metrics.baseline: 17 findings as_is and 19 synthetic_reference across 12 review records, with 3 high and 17 medium
metrics.control_limit: any critical or any high finding
metrics.definition: The count of findings at each severity raised by one review pass, per profile.
metrics.formula_or_rule: count(findings at severity) per review pass
metrics.metric_name: Finding severity profile per review pass
metrics.target: 0 critical and 0 high; medium trending down review over review

metrics.action_on_breach: Either the action is not addressing the risk, or the scoring is not honest. Raise a PIM.3 proposal to determine which.
metrics.baseline: 0 of 6 moved; three entries have residual exposure equal to inherent because no action has been taken
metrics.control_limit: no movement across two consecutive reviews for any entry with a done action
metrics.definition: The number of risk entries whose residual exposure fell between consecutive reviews, over the number of entries with a taken action.
metrics.formula_or_rule: count(residual exposure lower than at the previous review) / count(entries with an action whose status is done)
metrics.metric_name: Risk exposure movement per review cycle
metrics.target: at least half of the entries with a taken action show a lower residual exposure at the following review

metrics.action_on_breach: The instance count is too small for a percentage to mean anything at this volume. Below the first 20 instances this metric is reported as a raw count and not as a percentage.
metrics.baseline: 100 percent over 6 instances, each with exactly one non-conformance recorded
metrics.definition: The number of performed process instances judged conforming against the process's own acceptance criteria, over the number of instances. 'partially_conforming' counts as not conforming.

observations.derivation: Counted by reading the disposition_reason field of each corrected entry in governance/coverage-plan.json and recording the number that had been marked mapped with no backing record. Each entry names the check that found it false.
observations.source_of_the_synthetic_fiction: The finding is real work against the real corpus. The number 13 is a factual count of corrections this process performed and is not invented.

observations.derivation: Counted from the generated requirement-to-test coverage matrix, taking the count of rows whose status is UNCOVERED. 48 requirement artifacts in total across both profiles.
observations.source_of_the_synthetic_fiction: The counts are read from the corpus. What is synthetic is the forward target, not the baseline.

observations.derivation: Computed as (48 - 41) / 48 * 100 = 14.58, rounded to 15. Recorded as 16 against the 7 FSR denominator used by the generated coverage output, which counts only functional safety requirements. The two denominators are different and both are recorded because a reader comparing them would otherwise conclude one is wrong.
observations.source_of_the_synthetic_fiction: The arithmetic is real; the choice to publish two denominators is the author's and is itself a limitation of MET-02.

observations.derivation: Counted by reading execution_kind on every execution record in both profiles: 13 recorded as host or simulation runs, 12 as synthetic_fixture or none.
observations.source_of_the_synthetic_fiction: The count is real. The 13 host runs are runs of real foxBMS product code on a host, which is a real measurement of the real code; what is synthetic is any implication that they measure the target hardware.

observations.derivation: Counted from the finding arrays of all 12 review records: 17 in the as_is profile and 19 in the synthetic_reference profile.
observations.source_of_the_synthetic_fiction: The findings are real statements about the corpus. The counts are arithmetic on them.

observations.derivation: Counted the performed_instances arrays across the six supporting-process records authored in this pass. Each carries exactly one instance and each instance records exactly one non-conformance.
observations.source_of_the_synthetic_fiction: The instances are authored. They are fictional occurrences with fictional participants and they exist to show what a populated process record looks like, not because anything happened.

revision_history.description: Measurement plan authored because MAN.6 was recorded as partially_mapped with the reason that no measurement plan existed. The 100 quantified acceptance criteria on requirement records are product verification criteria, not a process measurement plan; this record adds the population, the collection rule, the baseline, the target, the control limit, the analysis method and the ownership that a process measurement plan requires.

record_verbatim.separation_from_product_evidence: Every metric in this plan measures the development process. None of them measures the product's behaviour, and none of them carries product verification credit. A metric that reaches 100 percent says the project's records are complete and honest; it says nothing about whether the battery management system is safe. The corpus-wide product evidence dimension is computed separately and is zero for target hardware, and the two numbers must never be added together or quoted in the same sentence without this sentence.

shape_note: Deliberately not shaped like a corpus record: no top-level id, profile, artifact_type or source_refs, so that generating packets cannot change any coverage number. See the module docstring of make_review_packets.py.

_contract.digest_note: The digests below are already filled in. Copy them; do not type them. Run `make_review_packets.py --transcribe FB2-MAN-MSM-000001` to have them printed as a pasteable block.
_contract.grant_is: any value other than "pending" or absent
required_elements: 2. approved_by - a named individual, not a role and not a team

3. role - a role_id declared in role-and-review-policy.json#/roles - plus independence{owner_role, satisfied, evidence, policy_ref}; the approving role must differ from owner_role AND from the author of the last content revision
4. date - ISO-8601, checked by grammar and by parse

5. review_packet{path, sha256, record_sha256_at_signing}; path must resolve to a packet.json on disk under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed ONLY - the regenerated tree docs/artifacts/reviews/packets is NOT admissible, because it is rewritten on every regeneration and would destroy your evidence; sha256 must equal that file's bytes now; record_sha256_at_signing must equal this packet's integrity.record_sha256; target.record_id and target.profile must both name this record

6. approval_ledger_ref{ledger_id, entry_sha256} naming your entry in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. It is approval METADATA, not content: it is excluded from the record's content digest and is never a revision_history entry, so recording it neither bumps the revision nor stales a link. NEVER record the approval in revision_history - doing so stales every link pinning this revision and invalidates every stored review digest. See docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md

signature_block._packet_sha256_note: The digest of this packet.json's own bytes. It is deliberately left null rather than filled, because a file cannot contain its own digest. Compute it with `shasum -a 256`, or use `--transcribe`, which resolves it.
signature_block._recording: Archive the signed packet under docs/artifacts/reviews/signed/<profile>/<id>.json, then record the approval as human_approval_status plus an approval_evidence.human_approval block on the record, plus approval_ledger_ref naming one appended line in docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl. Do NOT add a revision_history entry: see docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.md.
signature_block._rule: Empty by construction. No automated process may fill this. Filling it in is the only thing that changes human_approval_status on the record. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus rule human_approval_rejected is an EVIDENCE requirement, not a prohibition: a properly evidenced approval is ACCEPTED and keeps `corpus.py check` green, while a bare grant value is still rejected. What the validator reads is contract.approval_evidence_block below; it fails if any of its six elements is missing, and the finding names which.

signature_policy: The signature block below is empty by construction. This tool has no code path that writes a decision, an approval, a signature or an execution verdict. Filling it is a human action. As of 2026-10-04 (amendment APPROVAL-RULE-A1) the corpus ACCEPTS a properly evidenced approval rather than banning the value outright, so this rule now has to carry the evidence contract in full: see signature_block._contract. Since the same day (amendment APPROVAL-LEDGER-A1) the approval is recorded in the append-only ledger at docs/artifacts/governance/approval-ledger.jsonl and the record keeps only a reference to it, so recording your signature neither bumps the revision nor invalidates any review digest.
